_comment: Carry destination for issue #962, the round-4 audit. The stage that needs
this is any later seat that audits or re-verifies the Home Assistant
quality-scale register. Shape and required fields:
stage: any later seat that audits or re-verifies the quality-scale register (the D10 dimension of a later round; tools/audit/briefs/D10.md is its method, tools/audit/round4/D10/qs_rules.py its harness)

carries.from: the pull request that added the manifest's quality_scale key and flipped the register's docs-examples row when the owner's Blueprints Exchange listing went live
carries.control: Two properties, each measured with the perturbation that would have made it fail. FIRST: no instrument, in this tree or upstream, notices a declared tier the register does not support. Measured at the merge base by adding a tier the register did not support to custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json and running every script the scoped gate selects for that file -- tests/deployment_shape.py and tests/entities.py both exited zero, tests/env_drift.py and tests/golden.py produced byte-identical output with and without the key, and no file under tests/ or tools/ reads the key at all. The real hassfest agrees: script.hassfest validate on the package exits zero for any tier name in its enum, because validate_iqs_file returns on `if not integration.core` before it ever compares a manifest tier against quality_scale.yaml; the null control that proves that run was not vacuous is a value outside the enum, which is the only thing that made it exit non-zero. SECOND: tests/entities.py now derives the highest cumulative tier from the register's own rows and refuses a manifest that disagrees. Its controls, each failing on exactly that check and nothing else: the key removed, a tier below the derived one, a tier above it, a non-scaled value hassfest also accepts, and a register row regressed to todo.
carries.remeasure: Do not read the manifest's tier as an independent claim and do not re-derive it by hand -- it is a function of quality_scale.yaml, and tests/entities.py refuses any disagreement, so the two cannot differ on a green tree. Audit the ROWS instead. One row is not answerable from the tree at all: docs-examples rests on the owner's listing in the home-assistant.io Blueprints Exchange, and this suite has no network -- which is why tests/run.sh excludes tests/nightly_status.py -- so the row is pinned against the listing URL as a literal and nothing goes red if the post is unlisted. Re-fetch that URL yourself, from the register row's own comment, and check that it still resolves inside the Blueprints Exchange category and still links the files under blueprints/automation/. The address without its /t/ path segment is a 404, so use the form the row cites. qs_rules.py continues to report the row unmeasured for the same reason, so its divergence count will not tell you.
carries.brief: Auditing the quality-scale register: the manifest now declares a tier, and it is derived rather than transcribed. tests/entities.py walks the tiers in order, stops at the first tier holding a row short of done or exempt, and refuses a custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json that names anything else, so a divergence between the two is not a finding available on a green tree -- audit the rows. hassfest cannot help: validate_iqs_file returns early for a custom integration, so the key is checked against a list of legal tier names and nothing more, and a tier the register does not support passes it. The row that needs a human is docs-examples, whose bar is a listing in the home-assistant.io Blueprints Exchange. No gate script can see a forum, so that row is pinned against its URL as a literal and its liveness is carried by a dated verification in the row's comment rather than by any check. Re-fetch it, and confirm it still links the blueprints under blueprints/automation/, before you record that row as satisfied.
